what: Jansen walking linkage. One motor drives two Jansen-topology legs with their cranks half a turn apart. Yellow and orange rigid right-angle links combine three closed loops into a sweeping foot path. A real Technic stand supports the machine so that the complete path is visible. This is a gait laboratory; free walking on the floor is not claimed.
try: Open Examples and choose Dune Strider, then open the model with its program. The model, Code and Blocks load together. Press Reset, then Run. Reset again before repeating or after manual movement; keep manual overrides off during the experiment.

Observe the bounded initial return to datum, two forward crank revolutions, the short pause, and two reverse revolutions back to datum. The final state is hold. A watchdog stops the experiment after 85 seconds if it does not complete.

Follow the last hole of each coloured toe beam. Compare its nearly level lower passage with its raised return. The nominal analytical full path is about 71.54 mm wide and 10.23 mm high; compare that prediction with the two visible foot paths.
Notice that both legs have the same path, separated by 180 degrees of crank phase. Half-turn phasing is a rigid shaft property; the program sends commands to only one motor.
why: The crank radius is two studs and the two grounded rocker lengths are four studs. Each crank-to-rocker connecting rod spans five studs. Their common four-stud ground separation makes both primary loops Grashof crank-rockers: shortest plus longest is 2+5=7, while the remaining sum is 4+4=8. The one-stud inequality margin permits a full input turn. A further five-stud connecting rod closes onto the four-stud edge of the lower rigid right-angle link. That third closure is checked separately: Grashof alone is not a proof for the whole eight-link mechanism.
matters: A constant-speed rotary input can generate a useful non-circular path without independently controlling the foot. The same principle underlies linkage walking machines. This model adapts the topology to stock Technic hole spacing and rigid right-angle assemblies; it does not reproduce Theo Jansen's optimized original proportions.
question: If you increase both two-stud crank radii to three studs while keeping the four-stud ground and rockers and the five-stud rods, can the input still be treated as a safely continuous crank?
answer: No. The primary-loop Grashof sums become 3+5=4+4=8, the change-point boundary. Collinear configurations can lose a unique assembly branch and jam under real tolerances. The lower loop and part clearances also need new checks. Do not treat the current model's qualification as evidence for that rebuild.
further: An eight-link planar mechanism with ten equivalent revolute pairs has nominal mobility 3(8-1)-2(10)=1. The two legs share one crank shaft, so the complete display still has one controlled degree of freedom.

A seven-hole straight beam has a six-stud endpoint span. The five-stud binary rods here use holes h0 and h5, leaving one hole beyond the moving joint. Read the placement and interface ledgers before substituting a beam.

The near 10L and far 9L anchor shafts are fixed to the stand by cross-hole keys secured with two pins. Frictionless pins carry the moving leg joints; black friction pins fasten the rigid right-angle assemblies. The near anchor also supports the front drive-bearing bridge. Colour is a visual cue, but the actual part number determines the joint type.

The physical frame is free on the simulation floor. Output positions are measured relative to its observed pose, and the validation checks frame tilt, hinge closure, body ownership and return. No foot path is assigned by the physics observer.
The analytical curve is not a physical build test. Real pin friction, backlash, axle torsion, cable routing and tolerances remain untested until the machine is assembled in hardware.

Compare Stride Lab's single Hoeken-type four-bar with these three coupled loops. Inspiration: Theo Jansen's own Chorda-period account, https://www.strandbeest.com/evolution?period=chorda. No source CAD, images or instructions are copied.
formula: Units: studs. O=(0,0), A=(-4,0), B=2(cos q,sin q); AC=AD=AE=4; BC=BD=EF=5; DF=4; DG=5. E-A=R90(C-A), G-D=(5/4)R90(F-D). The second crank uses q+pi. Grashof margin=(4+4)-(2+5)=1 stud.
